purpose: Skeleton-first forearm audit. Determine whether the radius and ulna should be re-targeted independently of the short r95 forearm surface.

current_a003.note: The osteometric proxies come from the existing a003 review addendum and include explicit endpoint allowances; they are more appropriate than raw control-stick span for stature-equation comparison.

stature_conditioned_ansur_chain.interpretation: At 1.82 m stature, the ANSUR component chain implies a radiale-stylion span of about 278 mm. The a003 radius osteometric proxy is about 31 mm shorter. This is consistent with the previously observed short distal upper-limb surface.

independent_ct_crosscheck.caution: The CT radius definition ends at the wrist midpoint, not the styloid, and the cohort's mean stature is not reported. Therefore this source is a plausibility check only, not a canonical length target.

ulna_secondary_stature_check.caution: Percutaneous olecranon-tip to styloid-tip measurement is population-specific and not identical to the a003 proxy. It is a weak directional cross-check only.

findings: The radius should remain REOPEN for canonical retargeting. The stature-conditioned ANSUR chain implies a longer radiale-stylion span than the current a003 osteometric proxy by roughly 31 mm.

The ulna should NOT simply be lengthened by the same amount. Available CT and percutaneous sources use different endpoints and populations; the current ulna proxy is closer to several adult reference values than the radius is.

Therefore the skeleton-first rebuild must treat radius and ulna as distinct bones with independent endpoint definitions, while preserving their proximal/distal radioulnar joint congruence and pronation-supination axis.
The old mesh-fit assumption of a single forearm segment is explicitly rejected for final canonical proportions.
next_steps: Derive a canonical radius corridor from stature-conditioned ANSUR plus at least one endpoint-compatible male CT/osteometric dataset.
Derive a canonical ulna corridor with explicit olecranon/styloid endpoint semantics; do not infer it from radius by a fixed ratio.
Rebuild distal radioulnar and wrist landmarks from the canonical bone endpoints before accepting carpal positions.
Re-run pronation/supination tests after the canonical radius/ulna/wrist geometry is instantiated.
